name: Ring Isomorphism
reason: Distinct new row (no ring-isomorphism in atlas or in the screened candidates). Kayal-Saxena prove Ring Isomorphism (are two finite rings, given by structure constants, isomorphic?) is in NP INTERSECT coAM and is at least as hard as Graph Isomorphism -- a genuine candidate NP-intermediate problem, unlikely NP-complete (coAM-hard NP-complete would collapse PH). Directly parallel to how the atlas already treats graph-isomorphism and group-isomorphism (both decision=NPI-candidate). Garden cites [KS05]; web-verified.

charges_established.citation: Neeraj Kayal & Nitin Saxena, On the Ring Isomorphism & Automorphism Problems, 20th IEEE Conf. on Computational Complexity (CCC) 2005 (ECCC TR04-109; journal version 'Complexity of Ring Morphism Problems', Comput. Complexity 15 (2006) 342-390) -- proves Ring Isomorphism in NP INTERSECT coAM and >= Graph Isomorphism

name: Ring Automorphism
reason: Distinct new row and a decision-vs-search DECOUPLING (cf. the atlas primality-vs-factoring pair). Kayal-Saxena prove the Ring Automorphism DECISION problem (does a finite ring have a nontrivial automorphism?) is in P -- nontrivially, and in contrast to Graph Automorphism (GI-hard) and to Ring Isomorphism (NP INTERSECT coAM). The SEARCH version (exhibit a nontrivial automorphism) is equivalent to integer factoring. Established, cited, non-obvious. Web-verified.

charges_established.citation: Neeraj Kayal & Nitin Saxena, On the Ring Isomorphism & Automorphism Problems, CCC 2005 (ECCC TR04-109) -- proves existence of a nontrivial ring automorphism is decidable in P; FINDING one is factoring-equivalent (decision/search decoupling)

name: Stochastic Games (Simple Stochastic Games)
reason: Distinct new row -- NOT the existing 'Stochastic SAT' candidate (that is PSPACE-complete SSAT). Condon's simple-stochastic-game value problem (White/MAX, Black/MIN, and random Nature move a token; does White have a strategy reaching the target with probability >= 1/2?) is in NP INTERSECT coNP and not known in P, a candidate NP-intermediate problem in the exact mold of the atlas's factoring (also NP INTERSECT coNP => decision=NPI-candidate). NOTE: the Garden entry gives NO citation ('in NP INTERSECT coNP, P?'); Condon 1992 supplied from the standard reference and web-verified.

charges_established.citation: Anne Condon, The complexity of stochastic games, Information and Computation 96(2) (1992) 203-224 -- proves the simple-stochastic-game value problem is in NP INTERSECT coNP. AGENT-SUPPLIED (not cited in the Garden entry); web-verified

name: k-Local Hamiltonian
reason: Bona fide decision problem (is the smallest eigenvalue of a sum of m k-local Hamiltonians < a or > b?) and the CANONICAL QMA-complete problem. The atlas decision vocabulary has NO quantum (QMA) rung, so this is admissible-but-unexpressible -- a missing-decision-rung gap exactly like the flagged sum-of-radicals case. Owner ruling needed. Also carries a full k=2 classification [CM16], Cubitt-Montanaro.

charges_established.citation: Kitaev, Shen & Vyalyi, Classical and Quantum Computation (AMS 2002) [k=5]; Kempe & Regev, 3-Local Hamiltonian is QMA-complete, Quantum Inf. Comput. 3 (2003) [k=3]; Kempe, Kitaev & Regev, The complexity of the local Hamiltonian problem, SIAM J. Comput. 35 (2006) 1070-1097 [k=2] -- all cited by the Garden as [KSV02],[KR03],[KKR04]

name: Quantum k-SAT
reason: Quantum analogue of SAT (is there a state annihilated by all k-qubit projector terms / satisfying the frustration-free promise?). QMA_1-complete for k>=3, while quantum 2-SAT is in P (Bravyi). Admissible-but-unexpressible: the atlas has no quantum (QMA/QMA_1) rung. Owner ruling needed. Garden gives no formal citation ('QMA-complete for k=3', links a lecture); Bravyi 2006 supplied.

charges_established.citation: Sergey Bravyi, Efficient algorithm for a quantum analogue of 2-SAT, arXiv quant-ph/0602108 (2006) (Contemp. Math. 536 (2011) 33-48) -- quantum k-SAT QMA_1-complete for k>=3, quantum 2-SAT in P. AGENT-SUPPLIED (Garden cites only a lecture)

name: Group Non-Membership
reason: Black-box group problem (given a multiply/invert oracle and elements g,h1..hk, is g NOT in <h1..hk>?); Watrous proves it is in QMA. Admissible-but-unexpressible: the atlas has no quantum rung. IMPORTANT: this is a MEMBERSHIP result (in QMA), not QMA-completeness, so even whether it is 'admissible' is itself an owner call. Owner ruling needed.

charges_established.value: in QMA (membership, not completeness) [UNEXPRESSIBLE: no atlas quantum rung]
charges_established.citation: John Watrous, Succinct quantum proofs for properties of finite groups, FOCS 2000 [Wat00] -- Group Non-Membership in QMA

name: Equality (communication complexity)
reason: As a COMPUTATION, EQ(x,y)=[x=y] is trivially in P; its rigorous established complexity lives in COMMUNICATION complexity (deterministic CC = Theta(n), fooling-set/rank lower bound). The atlas has no communication-complexity CHARGE AXIS, so this is admissible-but-unexpressible -- but note this is a missing-AXIS gap (an entire new charge column), NOT the QMA missing-decision-rung gap. Whether communication complexity is in scope is squarely an owner decision. Flagged rather than silently rejected because EQ is the canonical problem of a major resource model.

charges_established.citation: Yao, Some complexity questions related to distributive computing, STOC 1979 (model); Kushilevitz & Nisan, Communication Complexity (Cambridge, 1997) -- fooling-set/rank lower bound for EQ

name: Unique k-SAT
reason: PROMISE problem (each instance has 0 or exactly 1 satisfying assignment) -- excluded by the standard ('class/promise-problem rather than a problem'). The cited [CIK+03] result is an exponential-time-hypothesis-style equivalence (Unique-k-SAT in 2^{eps n} for all eps => k-SAT likewise), a subexponential-time statement, not one of the 8 charges.
